entries.title: sUNC, crisper text, a font repair command, and two more panels you can move
notes: !sunc scores this executor against sUNC's own 86 checks -- the same 86, name for name, so the number is comparable with what sunc.su gives you. 83 of them call the function for real and check what comes back. The other three say on the row why they cannot: debug.setstack would crash the client, replicatesignal reaches the server, and WebSocket.connect opens a socket to somebody else's host.

Two guards in the test suite keep that honest and fail the build otherwise: every check must be able to fail for a reason rather than only by throwing, and every check is run against a function that exists and does nothing -- precisely the fake sUNC was built to catch -- and must refuse it. That second rule caught two checks of my own that were presence tests in disguise; they now say so instead of passing.

Checks whose real test would do something to the game or the network -- fireclickdetector, request, WebSocket.connect -- score half and the row says exactly why they were not run. Counting an unverifiable pass as a pass is the arithmetic sUNC exists to replace.

The panel is draggable, collapsible and closable. Each check expands as it runs to show what it found and collapses as the next one starts, the log follows along, and the ring spins while there is no honest number to show before counting up to the score. Category tabs appear when it finishes: picking one re-animates the ring to that category alone, and it opens on All with the full score so you can inspect afterwards.

Run custom picks what to test -- searchable, whole categories tick at once, and you can add function names of your own. Copy and Save write the full report. Re-opening !sunc shows the last run for this executor; a saved run from a different executor is ignored rather than shown with a caveat.

The sweep is paced to a fixed twelve seconds however many checks are in it, rather than a fixed step per check -- a custom run of five is no longer over before you have read one, and every row finishes opening before the next asks it to close.

!rexec now says what actually came back when it cannot fetch a build -- a 404 page, a rate-limit notice, a truncated response and a dead connection all used to report the same sentence. It also retries without the cache-busting query string, which is what makes every fetch miss the CDN.

Fixed sUNC reporting every check as "not defined": the lookup used rawget on the script environment, and several executors hand the script a proxy whose __index forwards to the real globals -- rawget walks straight past it. It now indexes normally and searches the script environment, getgenv() and _G in turn, since executors do not all inject into the same table.

Text is no longer pixellated at small sizes. Roblox rasterises a glyph atlas at whole pixel sizes -- ask for 13.5 and it rasterises at one size and scales to another. Two steps of the type scale were fractional (13.5 and 11.5), which is every row title and every grey sub line in the interface. Both are whole numbers now.

The workspace font viewer showed one weight because that is all it ever built: a .ttf holds one face, and the viewer staged the single file you clicked and declared it Regular 400 whatever it actually was.

It now reads the weight out of the filename and gathers every font file beside it that belongs to the same family, so opening any one of Manrope's six weights previews all six -- each line rendered in its own weight, lightest first, with the one you clicked in white. The size samples use the weight you opened rather than the family default.
The preview scrolls, since a family is any number of weights and the pane is 80px tall on a phone.

!fixfont checks the font files on disk, repairs what a re-download can fix, and says which of the three causes rough text actually is -- damaged files, an executor that will not load them, or an executor whose renderer is simply worse at a font it has to rasterise itself. Damaged files were invisible before: the only check was that the file existed, so a truncated download stayed broken for good.
!fixfont builtin swaps to Roblox's own font, which is baked into the client and always draws sharp. !fixfont manrope goes back. The choice is remembered.

The ESP window is now a floating panel like the aim one -- draggable, collapsible to a strip that says how many features are drawing, closable, and it stays where you leave it. Refresh and Clear moved inline.

The aim panel's mode description and bind hint were drawn on top of each other. Fixed, its rows now sit on the same cards the rest of the hub uses, and ESP is one click away from it since the two are used together.

entries.title: One workspace, several accounts
notes: Sign in on a second Roblox account and the hub asks once, before anything else: keep using the config that is already here, or set this account up as new. It shows both accounts side by side -- the one that saved it, with when it was last used, and yours, marked NEW.

Set up as new gives that account its own config file. Theme, prefix, keybind, saved scripts and Spotify sign-in all start clean, and the other account's config is left exactly as it was -- this starts one, it does not take one over.
Tick remember and every account after that is handled the same way without asking. The notification that applies it has a Change button, so it is not a decision you make once and cannot find again.

Asked once and only once. Agreeing is recorded per account rather than by moving ownership, otherwise two accounts on one machine would prompt each other on every other boot. After the answer, the guide or the resume prompt gets its turn as normal -- which of the two depends on what you picked.

entries.title: The aim panel is a panel
notes: The aim window is now draggable, collapsible and closable, and it stays where you leave it between sessions -- the same floating panel the Spotify card and the workspace editor use.
Clicking a mode, a toggle or a colour used to close the window. It was a modal, and changing anything in it rebuilt it from scratch; now only the contents redraw and the window stays put.
!aimbot, !silentaim and !aimassist switch an already-open panel instead of closing it, and re-arm silent aim's hook when you switch into it.

entries.title: Aim
notes: !aim opens a panel with three modes behind one target picker: Assist nudges your aim, Lock holds the camera while you hold the bind, and Silent never moves the camera at all. !aimassist, !aimbot and !silentaim open straight into one of them; !unaim turns it off.

Field of view as a real circle on screen, which turns accent when it has somebody. Smoothness, prediction, team check, wall check, and colour pickers for the circle and the target line -- through the same picker the ESP colours use.
Smoothing is framerate independent. A fixed per-frame lerp snaps twice as hard at 120fps as at 60, which is the difference between an assist and an obvious lock depending on whose machine it runs on.

It targets whoever is nearest your CROSSHAIR rather than nearest to you -- the one you were already closest to pointing at is the one you meant -- and sticky keeps that target while you hold, so somebody crossing in front cannot steal your aim mid-shot.
Prediction leads their velocity and is off by default: leading a hitscan shot is a miss.
Wall check is off by default because it costs a raycast per player per frame, and the panel says so rather than leaving you to find out.

Silent aim is honest about its limits. It answers the game's own hit test rather than moving anything, which only works where the game asks in a way a metamethod hook can reach -- the mode description says so, and an executor that cannot hook says so on the spot instead of failing quietly. Both hooks check the caller so they never lie to the hub's own code, and only answer while you are actually holding the bind with a target.
Settings, bind and colours persist, and are type-checked on the way back off disk -- the config is a file anything can edit.
The slider moved onto UI, so the Spotify scrubber, the volume and every numeric setting here are one implementation of "drag a value between two ends" rather than three.

entries.title: A workspace editor
notes: !workspace (or !files, !editor, !explorer, !fs) opens a file manager for the executor's WHOLE workspace, not just unihub's corner of it. Draggable, collapsible, closable, and it remembers where you put it.

Browse with clickable breadcrumbs, filter the current folder as you type, and open a file to read it. Text files open in an editable box with Save; images render; anything else says why it cannot be shown rather than showing an empty pane.
Create a file with its contents and extension, make folders, rename, duplicate, and run a .lua straight from the tree.
It opens on unihub, because that is what anyone opening it from inside the hub is looking for. The workspace root is one click up, and it remembers where you were after that.

Deleting goes through the same staged confirm the config wipe uses -- it names the full path, says how many items are inside a folder, and waits before the button arms. This reaches every other script's data and nothing here goes to a bin.

Rename is copy-then-delete in that order, so a failed write leaves the original rather than nothing. New names cannot contain a slash: a file goes in the folder you are looking at, not wherever the name says.

Every action is gated on the specific function it needs -- an executor with readfile but no delfile is common -- and one that cannot work is dimmed rather than hidden, so the row does not jump and you can see why.
There are no timestamps, because no executor exposes a stat. Size, kind and extension are everything the filesystem will actually tell us, and a Modified column would have been a fabrication.

Built from the parts that already existed: the shared gradient buttons, the modal, the drag easer, the chrome buttons, and the momentum scroller -- which moved off the Spotify panel onto UI so both use one copy.

Copy became copy-then-paste: pick a file up, open any folder, put it down. It used to duplicate in place, which is the one thing you can already do by pasting without moving. Plus a Path button that copies the full path.

The action row wraps instead of running off the edge. gradButton ships at width 10 and expects the caller to size it, so the wrap check was comparing every button against 10 and Delete sat outside the panel.
Code reads as code: no wrapping, a line-number gutter, and sideways scrolling. A minified JSON wrapped to the pane was one grey paragraph with no structure in it.

The editor shows a cursor. A TextBox with transparent text hides its caret and its selection too, so the highlighted overlay made it impossible to see where you were typing -- it now shows colour while you read and plain text the moment you click in.
Selecting a file no longer rebuilds the whole tree. Two rows retint; the list stays put and keeps its scroll and hover.
Reading a file shows a progress bar. readfile blocks, so the work yields a frame first -- otherwise the bar is shown and hidden without ever being drawn.
A file with an extension nothing recognises is opened raw and judged on its bytes. Refusing on the name hid every .conf, .bak and extensionless file that was perfectly readable.
First-seen and last-edited times per file. Not created/modified: no executor exposes a stat, so those would be invented -- these are what the hub itself observed, and they are labelled that way.
Fonts get a type glyph rather than a shirt, and the panel rebuilds on a theme change like every other card -- owning its own ScreenGui meant nothing else was repainting it.
!refreshconfig re-reads the config from disk and rebuilds, so a change made in the workspace editor two commands over does not need the whole hub re-executed.

Cut, with a scissors glyph. Same clipboard as Copy with a flag; pasting moves, writing the destination before removing the source, and the row dims while it is in flight rather than vanishing on a move you can still cancel.
The breadcrumb trail is also a text field -- click the end of it and type a path. A path that is not a folder is refused rather than silently landing you somewhere else.

Folders can be selected, and therefore deleted. delfolder was wired up from the start, but clicking a folder navigated into it, so a folder could never be the selection and Delete was unreachable for every one of them. Click selects, click again enters, the chevron goes straight in.
JSON auto-formats on open, and the button became the way back: Unformat minifies, Format lays it out again.

Deleting anything belonging to Universal Hub says so in the confirm -- which half comes back on the next execute and which does not -- and the tree marks those files with a dot so you know before you get that far.

An extension nothing recognises still gets an icon. Adding the 'unknown' kind without a glyph left every .bak, .qqq and extensionless file drawing nothing, which reads as a row that failed rather than a file of an unknown type.

Horizontal scrolling works. The momentum scroller replaced Roblox's native one and only ever drove the vertical axis, so the code view's sideways scrollbar did nothing -- shift-wheel and drag now move both.
The wheel sink moved onto UI and both panels claim it, so scrolling the workspace no longer zooms the game out either. Two panels can hold it at once without fighting over the binding.

entries.title: Spotify, connected once
notes: !configurespotify connects Spotify for good. Authorization Code with PKCE, so it renews itself in the background and you never paste anything again -- rather than a token that died after an hour.

PKCE means NO client secret. What sits in the config is a refresh token and a client ID; the hub trades them for a fresh access token a minute before each one lapses, and a 401 mid-session renews and retries instead of telling you to reconnect.
Spotify Premium is required, and the setup modal says so first -- for playback control, as always, and since February 2026 to hold a developer app at all.

Every link in setup has a copy button: the dashboard, the exact redirect URI, and the authorise link built from your Client ID. Paste the whole address bar back; the hub finds the code in it, and says 'access denied' rather than 'no code' when you press Cancel.
The setup fields use the same wash, corner and type as everything else in the modal. They were an opaque slab with a stroke that snapped on when focused, which read as a form bolted onto the design.
SHA-256 and base64url in Lua, because Spotify refuses PKCE's plain method. Verified against FIPS 180-4 vectors and RFC 7636's canonical challenge.

Spotify is a floating panel, not a card: !spotify opens it, you drag it where you like and it stays there, and it collapses to a strip -- cover, track, artist, 0:42 / 3:14. As a card it could only appear after the menu had opened and the column had reflowed, which is the lag it had in both directions.
Covers are real images -- fetched, written and served through getcustomasset, capped at 24 with the oldest evicted, cleared on disconnect.
Without opening the card: !play (resume, or search-and-play by name), !pause, !skip, !back, !vol, !np, !unspotify.

Migrated to Spotify's February 2026 API. PUT/DELETE /me/tracks, GET /me/tracks/contains and both /playlists/{id}/tracks endpoints were removed outright -- liking, the heart state, opening a playlist and adding to one all now use /me/library and /playlists/{id}/items. Search's maximum dropped from 50 to 10.

Now playing is rebuilt: the cover is lifted off the glass with a shadow, the artist is in accent rather than a second grey, and the scrubber runs along the bottom edge advancing every frame instead of twice a second. Transport is solid -- at 17px a stroked triangle is mostly hole -- and every glyph on the row, transport and toggles alike, is normalised to one ink height so a single size really does look level.
Whichever track is playing is marked in Queue, Search and Lists -- accent title, a rule down the edge, and a glyph that tells playing from paused.
A track change raises a toast with the cover in it, the way a player command shows the target's face.

Fixes from real use: the search magnifier sat after your text because UIPadding moves children as well as text; covers were JPEGs written into .png files, which some executors accept and some silently refuse, so some art rendered and some was a blank tile; one cover shared by several rows only ever reached the first of them; the queue showed the same track eight times; and add-to-playlist could send an empty uri list and come back as 'missing required field uris'.
Transport is solid, not hollow: at 17px a stroked triangle is mostly hole. All five glyphs are normalised to one ink height and centred, so a single size on one line really does look level.

Momentum scrolling on every list. Roblox scrolls in discrete jumps on a wheel and gives desktop no inertia at all; the wheel adds velocity and it decays per second rather than per frame, so a throw travels the same distance at 30fps as at 60. Collapsing and expanding animates rather than teleporting between two heights.
Lists no longer jump to the top mid-scroll: a track change repaints every row to move the live mark, and that was resetting the scroll position.
One toast per track, not two. Starting something from the menu announced it, then the poll saw a new track and announced it again -- the poll's version wins because it carries the cover.
The now-playing cover restores its glyph if Roblox refuses the image. Only the small tiles had that fallback, so the big one could sit as an empty rectangle.
The toast's small round slot squares off with rounded corners for album art, and stays a circle for a headshot -- a cover composed to fill a square was losing its corners to it.

Covers that were merely slow to decode were being written off. A single IsLoaded check at two seconds is now a signal plus an eight-second timeout, which is why the 72px card art kept failing while the 38px strip, asking a moment earlier, succeeded.

The like, list, shuffle and repeat glyphs are on the same optical grid as the transport, and the unliked heart is thick enough to survive being drawn at 17px -- it was under a pixel wide and read as missing rather than hollow.
Scrolling a list no longer zooms the game out from under you. The wheel reached Roblox's camera as well as the panel; it is sunk while the pointer is over it and released the moment it leaves.
Repeat-one carries a 1. Rotating a circular arrow 180 degrees to mean repeat-one is a circular arrow.
Like and add-to-playlist moved up beside the title. They sat under the album art, a long way from the transport, reading as part of neither.
The clock/weather card is back in the slot it has always had.

The panel shows itself when something starts playing and steps aside when nothing is; closing it by hand is respected until the track changes. Nothing was polling while it was shut, so it could never do that before.

The panel no longer appears on execute. A ScreenGui is Enabled by default, so building one and parenting an opaque panel into it put the panel on screen the moment the hub loaded -- built now means built, not shown, and auto-show ignores the first poll because something already playing when you execute is not an event.

Scrolling could lock up entirely. The wheel is sunk while the pointer is over the panel, and that was driven by MouseEnter/MouseLeave -- a Leave missed because the gui was disabled under the cursor, or a row destroyed mid-hover while a list reloaded, left the wheel sunk for the rest of the session with scrolling and zoom dead everywhere. It is recomputed from the cursor every frame now, so there is no state to get stuck in.

Shuffle, repeat and play/pause stopped flicking back off. Spotify applies these asynchronously, so the poll a third of a second later still reported the old value and overwrote what you had just pressed -- the value you set now wins for a short window, and yields the moment the server agrees.

The heart reflects your library again. /me/library/contains replaced /me/tracks/contains in February and returns a different shape; every plausible one is read, and 'could not tell' is no longer cached as 'not saved'.

Switching theme no longer freezes an open Spotify panel. Every other card is parented to the hub's own gui and dies with it -- this one owns its ScreenGui, so a rebuild left the old panel on screen with live handlers writing to instances nothing repaints. It is torn down first and put back the way it was.

entries.title: Fling that actually throws people
notes: Fling is rebuilt on the method from Universal Hub MAIN. It goes to them and drives your root through their head on alternating offsets, every frame, carrying a velocity the solver can only resolve by launching somebody. The old one spun you in place and hoped they walked into it.
!fling all works. Fling was never registered as a command that takes a crowd, so the token fell through to a name lookup and answered 'no one matched all' -- while the tips screen advertised it.

You come back. Each throw records where you were standing and returns you there before the next target, so a fling all does not end after one person with you out past the skybox. Stopping mid-throw puts you down too.
A bare !fling still means stand still and fling whoever touches you, which is the only thing the old one was ever good for. Give it a name or 'all' to go and get them.
The kill plane and the seated state are put back on stop, on !stopall, and on unload -- a fling interrupted halfway used to leave the whole game with no kill plane and no UI left to fix it.
Finding nothing is an answer, not a row: a sad face and 'Nothing found' centred in the drawer, at a size you can read, for a misspelt command as well as an empty search.
Scripts already running are greyed in the command bar with a badge, so you can see it before you press rather than after the bar has closed.
Picking a script no longer also runs what you typed as a command.
Three new player tokens, on every command that can take them: nearby (everyone within 100 studs), friends (everyone here off your friends list), and joined (whoever arrived last).

fling all no longer misses people. A throw that failed because they were respawning or had not loaded is retried instead of skipped, nobody is thrown twice, and dying halfway no longer ends the run -- it waits for you to come back and carries on.
Flinging someone already flung this run warns instead of restarting the whole job and abandoning everyone still queued.
A crowd token that names nobody says which one was empty -- 'No one is nearby', not 'no one matched nearby', which reads like a typo.
Fling's notification carries the target's headshot, like every other player command already did.
Fling takes a fourth word: seconds on each target, hinted in the bar like every other valued command. !fling all fly 4.

!sfling is its own command now. Standing still and flinging whoever touches you was a fling TYPE, which it never was -- it has no target, so a player, a crowd token and seconds each all meant nothing for it.
The suggestion list shows every token. It used to keep two while nothing was typed, which hid five of the seven behind already knowing the word.

!introvert (or !hermit, !antisocial, !avoidfriends) leaves the game the moment someone on your friends list joins. !extrovert turns it off, and so does unloading or !stopall -- it is the only thing here that acts on its own, so it cannot be left armed behind you.

Tokens no longer look like players in the suggestion list. Their tile was a circle -- which at that size is what a headshot is -- so a block of them read as a block of people wearing glyphs. Squared off, with a rule under the last one.

entries.title: Mobile, animation packs, and a bar that moves
notes: The bar drags anywhere and remembers where. Cards open downward, or upward when there is no room below.
Dragging has weight everywhere -- the bar, the activity panel and the script hub ease toward the pointer instead of welding to it.
Every card fits the screen it is on. Modals scale to the viewport, drawers to the room actually below them.
Touch: a labelled Commands pill that rides the card stack, tap-away to close the bar, and fly steers from the thumbstick.
Animation packs replicate -- the locomotion is driven through the Animator rather than by editing the Animate script, which only ever changed what you saw.
23 animation packs, resolved to their real animation ids. Twelve executor logos in Info.
vfly, fling, copy, walkto, follow, animpack, clearworkspace, fixanim, rexec.
Fetches carry a cache-buster, so a re-execute gets the newest build instead of the CDN's five-minute-old copy.
The camera's field of view is restored to whatever the game had, not a hardcoded 70.
Search ScriptBlox straight from the command bar: star a result, or open the hub already searched for it. Scripts never displace a command -- typing copy gets you the copy command.
!changelog, and a version that only moves when there is an entry explaining what moved with it.
The hub does not drag -- neither the bar nor the command bar. The floating panels (activity, script hub) still do, as they always have.
Command bar search shows a sweeping bar while it waits on ScriptBlox, and an empty bar offers the scripts you ran most recently -- from the hub or from the bar, same list.
Strings are encrypted now, not just locals renamed -- the published file has no readable text in it at all.
Script hub gains Running and Last used tabs; Last used follows you between games rather than resetting per place.
Command bar: searches the whole line, shows recents and scripts for this game, marks verified and key-locked ones, and says so when there are no results.

Every shipped asset is renamed uhub_*. The executor resolves getcustomasset by FILENAME, not by path, so three scripts each shipping a logo.png fought over the name -- which is why Infinite Yield wore our mark and our splash wore another hub's bird.

entries.title: LITE V2 -- rebuilt, not updated
notes: V2 is not V1 with features bolted on. The interface, the command pipeline and the storage were all rewritten.
One glass design system: every bar, chip, card and modal is built from the same treatment, so the whole thing reads as one product rather than a pile of scripts.
A real command bar -- ranked suggestions, player and mode tokens with aliases, argument hints, and Enter that knows whether to complete or run.
Cards instead of windows: clock, weather, performance, profile and settings all live in one stack that reflows around whatever is open.
Everything persists -- theme, prefix, keybind, favourites, positions, usage -- and survives a teleport.
Ships from GitHub with its own icons and font, downloaded once on first run.
Infinite Yield's command set imported wholesale, so V2 is a superset of what V1 could do.
